cands.bio: Democratic U.S. representative for California's 12th District since January 2025. Previously a BART board member (2016–2024, president from 2020), nonprofit executive (Young Women's Freedom Center, Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights, Rosenberg Foundation, Akonadi Foundation), and a 2003 MacArthur Fellow.

controversies.text: Missed 12 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.8%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 3, 2025-06-09 to 2025-06-09.

In March 2022 BART declared Simon's board seat vacant, saying she had moved outside her district. She said she moved after death threats tied to her police-reform work, and that BART officials had assured her the new address was in the district. Outside counsel found staff couldn't declare a vacancy. BART reinstated her and apologized. She later moved to Emeryville, inside the district.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association and California Environmental Voters.

2024 endorsements included Gov. Gavin Newsom, Rep. Barbara Lee, Attorney General Rob Bonta, EMILY's List, Giffords PAC, the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC and the San Francisco Chronicle editorial board.

cands.gaps: We found no statements or actions from her on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, growth limits or land conservation, Red Flag laws or suppressors, police pay and pensions, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so her 2024 survey answers are the most recent stated positions we have. We did not find when she moved within the Bay Area, since sources describe her as a lifelong resident. We could not confirm details of her BART tenure beyond her election, board presidency and the 2022 residency dispute.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.bio: Berkeley-based nonprofit executive and researcher. Former chief operating officer of IDEAS For Us, program co-lead of Democracy's Library at the Internet Archive, and founder of the Society Library nonprofit. Democratic candidate for U.S. House in California's 12th District in 2026. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists the We Persist voting group (Sway voting group by Tabitha) among her endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

In her Ballotpedia survey she says she was endorsed by Tristan Harris (AI and tech ethicist), Brewster Kahle (founder of the Internet Archive), Mark Graham (director of the Wayback Machine) and Kelly Erhart (environmental entrepreneur). This is the candidate's own statement.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Joyce grew up or when she moved to California. We found no stated positions or actions from her on data centers, property taxes, foreign or institutional purchases of homes and land, growth and development, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. Her campaign website text was cut off partway, and the pages it links to (the MAD Act text, background, district notes and endorsements list) were not available, so nothing from them is included. The endorsements shown come from her own survey answers and Ballotpedia, not from the endorsers' own pages.
